questions.question: Which feature gives Java runtime polymorphism?
questions.explanation: Overriding plus a parent-type reference lets the JVM choose the child's method while the program runs.

questions.question: Who decides which overloaded method is called?
options: The compiler, from the argument types
The JVM, from the actual object
questions.explanation: Overload resolution happens at compile time, which is why overloading is called static binding.

questions.question: What does this print? class Pay { String go() { return "P"; } } class Card extends Pay { String go() { return "C"; } } ... Pay p = new Card(); System.out.println(p.go());
questions.explanation: Dynamic method dispatch uses the real object, a Card, so Card's go() runs even through a Pay reference.

questions.question: What does this print? class Box { int size = 1; } class Crate extends Box { int size = 9; } ... Box b = new Crate(); System.out.println(b.size);
questions.explanation: Fields are not polymorphic. The declared type Box decides which field is read, so it prints 1.

questions.question: class Fare { } class BusFare extends Fare { int zones() { return 3; } } ... Fare f = new BusFare(); int z = f.zones(); Why does this fail to compile?
options: Fare does not declare zones(), and the compiler checks the reference type
You cannot store a BusFare in a Fare variable
questions.explanation: Through a Fare reference you can only call methods Fare declares. Downcast to BusFare after an instanceof check.

questions.question: What is upcasting?
options: Converting an int to a long
Storing a parent object in a child variable
Casting a String to Object with a runtime check
Storing a child object in a parent-type variable
questions.explanation: Upcasting, such as Payment p = new UpiPayment(), is always safe and needs no explicit cast.

questions.question: Object o = "ticket"; Integer n = (Integer) o; What happens when this runs?
questions.explanation: The compiler allows the downcast from Object, but the real object is a String, so the JVM throws ClassCastException.

questions.question: What does this print? class Pad { static String t() { return "pad"; } } class Tab extends Pad { static String t() { return "tab"; } } ... Pad x = new Tab(); System.out.println(x.t());
questions.explanation: Static methods are hidden, not overridden, so the call is bound to the declared type Pad.

questions.question: Which pair of methods is a valid overload?
options: int fee(int h) and long fee(int h)
void fee(int h) and void fee(int hours)
void fee(int h) and void fee(int h, int m)
static void fee() and void fee()
questions.explanation: Overloads must differ in their parameter lists. Return type, parameter names or static alone do not count.

questions.question: Why does adding @Override to a method help?
options: It makes the method run faster
It turns the method into an overload
It hides the parent method from subclasses
The compiler reports an error if no parent method matches
questions.explanation: Without @Override, a typo or wrong parameter type silently creates a new method instead of an override.
